producer_report.summary: `athena retry` now accepts a stale job. `athena go` on the retry merges the job's kept candidate onto the branch tip, from the base the candidate was built on. A clean merge is admitted, checked, replayed and verified again, and lands with no planner or producer run. A conflict starts a producer whose work tree is the conflicted merge, with the conflicting paths named in its brief. Its result is checked and verified in full, so nothing lands without a new verification. Root cause: D10 left out re-verification on the new base "until stale landings recur". Parallel jobs make them recur, but `earlier_attempt_with` refused stale jobs, so verified work was rebuilt from the request. Details: (1) reading.rs accepts `Closed(Stale)`, carries the stale outcome reason, lists stale in `retry_follow_up`, and prints a `stale` note on retry. (2) athena-git adds `Git::merge_tree_conflicts` and `MergedTree`. (3) run/mod.rs adds `stale_seed`, a `stale` flag on `ResumeSeed`, and the dispatch wiring. `stale_seed` falls back to retry-from-base unless the stale job has a candidate with no violations, a passing verification still matching its commit (`Verified::from_record`), and both commits still present. `resume_candidate` merges onto the new prediction commit when the flag is set, and closes failed if that merge conflicts or adds nothing. (4) briefs.rs: the reader brief says the job "went stale" and describes the merge instead of "was rejected" and "starts from the base". `RetrySeed.conflicts` drives a new producer section and working-directory text. (5) The stale outcome reason in close.rs now names `athena retry <id>`. (6) land.rs `plan()` is unchanged; a new test shows a merged candidate lands content with the verified fingerprint and that a differing fingerprint is still refused. (7) The retry help in main.rs now names stale jobs on its first line. (8) docs/decisions.md gets a new appended D157 that reverses D10's alternative (d), cites D10, and gives the parallel-jobs reason. The `git diff` shows only added lines. D157 avoids the phrases the backtest parser counts. (9) CHANGELOG has the entry. README no longer lists stale as refused and describes the stale retry.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test shows `athena retry` on a stale job returns a proposal instead of an error.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle retry_on_a_stale_job` passes. It makes a job stale with a user commit during verification, calls `Athena::retry` and asserts a Proposal with a reading and the request `try again on <job>`. The stale job is left unchanged. The core test in run/tests.rs also calls `retry` on a stale job. Before the change `earlier_attempt_with` bailed with `job … is stale; only a rejected or failed job…`.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test where the kept candidate merges cleanly onto a moved branch tip shows checks, replay and verification run on the merged tree, the job lands, and zero producer calls are recorded for the retry.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_stale_job_whose_candidate_merges_cleanly` passes. After the first go the counts are (planner 0, producer 1, verifier 1) and the outcome is Stale. After retry and go the counts are (0, 1, reader, 2): the producer count did not rise and the verifier count did. The UI lines include `resume     … went stale`, `candidate  `, `checks     ` and `replay     `. The job lands, README at HEAD has the candidate's text, and OTHER.md from the tip is kept, also in the candidate commit. The CLI test `the_reader_of_a_stale_retry_is_told_the_job_went_stale…` also asserts no producer ran for the retry.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test where the candidate conflicts with the moved tip shows the retry goes to a producer retry seeded from the kept candidate, and nothing lands without a new verification.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core --lib a_stale_job_whose_candidate_conflicts` passes. The tip rewrites the README lines the candidate also changed. Before the retry's go, README at HEAD does not contain the candidate's text. After go the counts are (0, 2, reader, 2): a second producer ran and the verifier ran again. That producer's work-tree README contains `<<<<<<<`, the tip's text and the candidate's text. Its prompt contains `## Retry: job <stale> went stale and its verified candidate conflicts with the branch tip` and the path `README.md`. The job lands only after the second verification, and the landed README has no markers.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test shows the landed content's fingerprint equals the fingerprint verified on the merged tree, and a landing whose verified fingerprint differs from the landed content is still refused (existing land.rs Plan::Stale tests still pass).

docs/decision-links.toml is out of scope, so D10 will not show as amended by D157 in the decision view. D157 avoids the phrases the backtest parser counts, so no unlisted supersession hit was created.

The stale path depends on the old candidate commit still being in the repository, as an unreferenced object. If it was collected, the retry falls back to the producer from the base, as before. I could not check the host's collection policy.

A producer that changes nothing in a conflicted work tree passes the conflict markers on to admission, checks and the verifier. The brief tells it to resolve every marker, and the verifier is the guard; I added no explicit marker check.

The first full `cargo test --locked` run exited 101 and I could not read its output. The later quiet workspace run passed everything, so I think the first failure came from running other cargo commands at the same time, but I did not confirm that.
mistakes: My first version of `carry` in reading.rs added Stale to the `failed` boolean that feeds `EarlierAttempt.failed`, which would have made the reader brief say a stale job "failed". I split it into a separate `stale` flag before testing.

I started the full `cargo test --locked` in the background and then ran other cargo commands, which probably contended with it. It exited 101 and I could not read why, so I had to rerun the workspace tests quietly in the foreground. That rerun passed everything.
learnings: Any file committed on the branch makes a job stale, not only governed-rule changes. `plan()` compares fingerprints of head and base, so a plain `OTHER.md` commit is enough in tests.
`Git::exit` returns `Exit { code, stdout, stderr }`. `merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` exits 1 on a conflict, prints the tree id first, then the conflicting paths until a blank line.
`Snapshot::create` with `SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree` accepts any commit's tree and hides records/ and private files, so a commit of a conflicted merge tree can seed a producer.
`Happened.reason` is None by default, so an early failure in `resume_candidate` must set `closing.happened.reason`, or the outcome reason reads `failed before verification`.
Bash here cannot read /tmp files, so a background cargo run's output cannot be inspected. Run tests in the foreground with `-q`.
desires: A way to read a background command's output file from inside the working directory, or a flag to write it there.
A wrapper that runs the full suite once with failures summarized, so a failure can be located without rerunning everything.
